_comment: HOSTING: all four archives are now served from the realm's own VPS at http://152.53.115.249/patches/ instead of GitHub releases. URLs are IMMUTABLE and carry the version in the filename -- the bytes behind a URL never change, so a player who started a download an hour ago can resume it safely, and rolling back is repointing at the previous filename (which is still on disk). The path field is what lands in the client and never carries a version: load order depends only on the archive letter. To publish a new version see PUBLISHING-PATCHES.md.
_comment2: MIRRORS: M and N are Trimitor's work and are NOT forked -- these are byte-identical copies of his release assets, still pinned to his tags, served from our host so that a deleted release or a dead repo cannot break new installs. The upstream each one came from is recorded in /srv/uncapped-patches/mirrors.tsv on the VPS, and a daily systemd timer (uncapped-mirror-check) reports when upstream ships a newer release carrying the same asset, or replaces the asset behind our pinned tag. Re-mirroring is always a deliberate act.

Caverns and Mines (microdungeons), the optional half of WDM. Only ships in Trimitor's BETA tags -- the newest tag in that repo is usually a -stable one that does not contain this file at all, which is why the drift checker compares against the newest release carrying this asset rather than the newest release.

Mount pack: mount models backported from Cata 4.3.4 + MoP 5.4.8 into 3.3.5a (1353 displays / 183 new models), plus CreatureModelData.dbc and CreatureDisplayInfo.dbc. 298 MB and effectively static. Deliberately NOT folded into the consolidated DBC bundle: merging them would mean re-uploading and re-downloading 298 MB for every one-line DBC tweak. Keeping it separate costs one extra manifest entry and saves that every single release.

_history: 2026-08-04: replaces patch-enUS-R (Spell/AreaTable/Map), patch-enUS-S (LightFloatBand, fog) and patch-enUS-4 (Item.dbc), and retires patch-enUS-5 -- which was inert, every spell id in it already being in R, and R winning load order anyway. Built by ADDING Item.dbc and LightFloatBand.dbc to a copy of R rather than repacking from a file list; a repack silently drops anything not on the list. Verified by hashing the effective post-load-order view of the whole patch stack before and after: 5756 reachable entries both sides, 0 lost, 0 changed, all 12 DBCs byte-identical.
_letter: U, not R. It has to sort after every archive it replaces -- and -S sorted AFTER -R. Reusing R would mean a client that had not yet pruned its old -S would load S's LightFloatBand.dbc over the consolidated one. Identical bytes today, so it would look fine; the day we change the fog it would silently serve the old fog instead. A letter past S cannot have that problem. V-Z stay free for a hotfix archive that needs to override this one.

_history4: 2026-08.08a: Spell.dbc ONLY -- the HASTE tooltips now say CRIT DAMAGE. Every haste tooltip therefore described a mechanic that does not exist here -- report #259 (Warrior Flurry) is the visible half. 126 spells / 171 Description+ToolTip fields relabelled, selected by AURA TYPE (the ten types the diverting handlers serve: 9, 65, 138, 140, 141, 192, 193, 216, 218, 252) intersected with player reachability (SkillLineAbility + Talent + SpellItemEnchantment + item_template.spellid_*, closed over EffectTriggerSpell), then extended by hand with the talent/glyph/summon rows whose TEXT quotes one of those auras ($8515s1% melee haste). ⚠ DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED, and each for a reason that is about the code not the wording: negative amounts (Thunder Clap, Curse of Tongues, Icy Touch, Frost Fever, Hurricane) still slow exactly as written; PET haste (Cobra Reflexes, Frenzy, Ghoul Frenzy) is real because a pet is a Creature and the IsPlayer() guard fails; creature enrages likewise; amounts >= 1000 hit SetInstantCast and return BEFORE the diversion; and haste RATING is diverted at a DIFFERENT rate (1000 rating = +1% crit damage, in Player::ApplyRatingMod), so hundreds of item/enchant/food tooltips still say 'haste rating' and need a separate decision. Report #151 is one symptom, not the bug: the STARTER mount 850139 'Mastiff (Dog Red)' (lua_scripts/starter_mount.lua, 167 characters) is simply the one of the 565 everybody owns. Measured on the live file before writing: 565/565 present in Spell.dbc, 565/565 carrying the mount auras, 0/565 with any SkillLineAbility row. 'These are mounts' is a measurement, not an assumption -- their effect/aura shapes are exactly Blizzard's two: effect=(6,6,0) aura=(78,32,0) x345 ground, same as spell 458 Brown Horse, and effect=(6,6,6) aura=(78,207,32) x220 flying, same as 32235. The 10219 pre-existing records are byte-identical and in the same order, and the string block is unchanged. Built by ADDING to 08.08a via StormLib, never repacked. verify-stack with M= and N= in BOTH stacks: 5757 -> 5758 reachable, 0 lost, 0 CHANGED bytes, exactly 1 newly reachable (skilllineability.dbc) which is the intent, other 12 DBCs byte-identical, PASS. _history6: 2026-08.08c: Spell.dbc -- the SAME 565 custom mounts can now be cast while moving. Cast-while-moving is a shipped realm feature with two halves that have to agree. The SERVER half (src/server/scripts/Custom/cast_while_moving.cpp:101) strips SPELL_INTERRUPT_FLAG_MOVEMENT (0x01, SpellDefines.h:26) from every cast-time spell at startup and the live log confirms it runs: 'Cast while moving: cleared movement interrupt on 13936 cast-time spell(s)'. The CLIENT half is this Spell.dbc, and it has to carry the same stripped flags because the client refuses the cast locally and never sends a packet -- which is why no server change could ever reach this. The 565 custom mount rows were authored separately and never went through the stripping pass. Report #292 ('you cannot mount the starter dog mount while moving, like every other mount') is the visible half via starter mount 850139. MEASURED, and this doubles as the proof that field 31 is InterruptFlags since no other field gives this answer: spells game-wide still carrying 0x01 = 565, and they are EXACTLY ids 850000-850564, with 0 anywhere else in the game. DISTRIBUTION: all 565 read 31 (0x1F) uniformly -- MOVEMENT|PUSH_BACK|INTERRUPT|AUTOATTACK|DAMAGE -- and all 565 become 30 (0x1E). The bit was MASKED OFF, not assigned: assigning 30 happens to agree today, but the other four bits are real and had to survive, and a future row that read something other than 31 would have been silently flattened. 30 is exactly what stock Brown Horse (458) and Golden Gryphon (32235) carry, so the 565 end up flag-identical to real Blizzard mounts rather than to a value we invented. BLAST RADIUS, measured by diffing the record block against 08.08b: 565 differing bytes, 565 rows, ONE distinct field touched (31), spell ids touched == exactly 850000..850564, string block byte-identical, record/field counts unchanged. Game-wide carriers of 0x01 afterwards: 0. Negative controls: Fireball 133, Heal 2054, Shadow Bolt 686, Wrath 5176 all keep 14 (0x0E) unchanged; Brown Horse 458 and Golden Gryphon 32235 keep 30; custom-but-not-a-mount Mending Fatigue 850565 keeps 0; fabricated filenames absent. Built by ADDING to 08.08b, never repacked -- the 08.08b SkillLineAbility.dbc survives byte-identical (sha256 3d3cd188589666a0..., all 565 SkillLine-777 rows still readable out of 08.08c). verify-stack with M= and N= in BOTH stacks, 08.08b -> 08.08c: 5758 reachable both sides, 0 lost, 0 newly reachable, exactly 1 file CHANGED (Spell.dbc) which is the intent, other 13 DBCs byte-identical including skilllineability.dbc. Cumulative published-08.08a -> 08.08c: 0 lost, 1 newly reachable (skilllineability.dbc), 1 changed (spell.dbc) -- exactly the two intended changes and nothing else. ⚠ verify-stack exits 1 on ANY byte change by design, so a Spell.dbc edit always reports FAIL; the check that matters is that the CHANGED list is exactly what you meant, same as 08.08a. NOTE the archive grew 16.1MB -> 20.6MB: replacing the 49.5MB Spell.dbc does not reclaim its old block. Content is correct; compacting stays a separate, deliberate change. _history7: 2026-08.14b: Lock.dbc ADDED (new to this archive) -- Stratholme drops from SEVEN player-facing keys to ONE. Locks 1079-1084 (the six postboxes) each gain item 12382 'Key to the City' as an ADDITIONAL accepted key; the original per-postbox key stays in slot 0, so the change is purely additive and cannot break anyone still holding one. WHY IT IS SAFE TO DO AT ALL: the six keys were never a set to complete -- every postbox independently summons three Undead Postmen and then Postmaster Malown eight seconds later (smart_scripts on 176346/176349/176350/176351/176352/176353), so any ONE key already got you the boss and the other five were redundant doors to the same encounter. Measured first: all six postbox keys drop from ONE mob, Stratholme Courier (11082), which has exactly one spawn, paying 3 keys per kill from three fixed pairs -- so a full set was ~4 clears and you could never target the one you were missing. Nothing consumes them and MaxCount is 0, so 189 dead keys had piled up across 29 characters. EXACT EDIT: 6 rows changed, file size identical at 51237 bytes, lock 1081 took slot 2 rather than slot 1 because its slot 1 holds a junk type=2/index=0 entry. verify-stack with M/N/Q in both stacks: 5758 -> 5759 reachable, 0 lost, 0 CHANGED bytes, exactly 1 newly reachable (lock.dbc) which is the intent. Negative control worth noting: none of M/N/Q carried Lock.dbc, so -U is only overriding the stock copy the edit was based on -- this is the check that was MISSED in 08.07a and caused the AreaTable regression. _history11: 2026-08.19b: Spell.dbc ONLY, 30 rows, DESCRIPTIONS ONLY -- no field that affects gameplay was touched. Food and drink tooltips now state the percentage they actually restore. ★ THE PROBLEM: FlatToPercent.Food.* has converted food to restore a SHARE OF YOUR POOL since it shipped, and the client never learned -- every food tooltip renders $o1, the stock flat number straight out of Spell.dbc, so a player with 57M health reads 'Restores 7500 health over 30 sec' and concludes food is worthless here. That cost real suggestion traffic: #195, #294 and #328 all asked for percentage food and were all FIXED, and then #939 arrived asking for it AGAIN, because nothing a player can see said it had happened. ★ THE WORDING IS EXACT, NOT A SIMPLIFICATION: FlatToPercent computes converted = amount * (pool / baseline) capped at 25%/5s, and early-outs when that is not GREATER than the authored amount -- so 'whichever is greater' is literally the code. The effective share is amount/baseline, independent of how large the pool grows. ⚠ THE SHARE IS LEVEL-DEPENDENT and every string says 'at level 80' out loud: baseline follows player_classlevelstats anchored to HealthBaseline80=25000 / ManaBaseline80=22000, so at 80 it IS that number for every class and the percentage is exact and class-independent, while at level 20 the same food is a much larger share of a much smaller baseline. A bare '5%' would have been a lie everywhere except 80. Standard level-80 food reads 5% per 5 sec, i.e. 30% of maximum health across its 30s duration. ⚠ DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED: the four food spells whose authored amount is 0 (the conversion early-outs, so their tooltips were already honest), and energy food -- GUARD 2 in FlatToPercent requires MiscValue == POWER_MANA because rogue/warrior food restores ENERGY, a fixed 100-point pool this realm never inflates; the script re-proves all 21 mana rows carry MiscValue 0 on every run rather than trusting a comment. ★ THE BASE WAS THE PUBLISHED 08.19a ARCHIVE, not a staging copy. Strings APPENDED and rows repointed, never edited in place (one offset is shared by many rows); string block 2392549 -> 2399096, record count unchanged at 50563. check_layout() re-verifies the aura id, the authored magnitude and the anchor substring of every one of the 30 rows before a byte is written, so a moved magnitude fails the build instead of shipping a stale percentage. verify-stack with M/N/Q in both stacks: 5760 reachable both sides, 0 lost, 0 newly reachable, exactly 1 CHANGED (spell.dbc), declared. Script: Server/azerothcore-wotlk/tools/dbc/patch_spell_20260819b_food_tooltips.py; durable copy at Launcher/work/Spell.20260819b.dbc.
_history13: 2026-08.30a: Spell.dbc ONLY, two reports' client halves. (1) #1141 ROGUE POISONS -- 29 tooltips, 'lasts for 1 hour.' -> 'lasts for 7 days.' The duration is computed in C++ (Spell::EffectEnchantItemTmp) where the shaman imbues and the warlock stones already sit at 7 days; the tooltip is a hardcoded string, not a $d token, so a server-only change leaves 29 tooltips lying -- the identical trap #975 documented. ★ THE ROW SET IS DERIVED FROM THE SAME RULE THE SERVER USES (SPELLFAMILY_ROGUE + SPELL_EFFECT_ENCHANT_ITEM_TEMPORARY) rather than a hand list, so the two cannot drift. ⚠⚠ 38615 'Bloodboil Poison' IS SPELLFAMILY_ROGUE AND IS EXCLUDED IN BOTH HALVES: it is a Black Temple mob poison, deliberately 30 minutes, and the only rogue-family enchant-temp row whose tooltip does not say '1 hour' -- which is how it was caught. Without the guard the C++ branch, which runs BEFORE the 30-minute switch, would have promoted a raid mechanic to seven days. _comment: THE PATCHED CLIENT EXECUTABLE. Stock 3.3.5a 12340 with LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE set and an import-table entry for UncappedCT.dll, which is what gets our code loaded before the client's entry point runs. Shipped whole rather than patched on the player's machine: every install then runs a byte-identical binary we can verify by hash, instead of the output of patch logic running on 40 different machines. The path is the RENAMED name the launcher's client hardening uses -- ClientHardening deletes a stock Wow.exe when this file is present, so the install ends up with exactly one runnable client.
_note: Not in payload/ and never committed: it is a modified Blizzard binary, and the payload tree is a public git repo.

_comment: THE INJECTED RUNTIME. A HARD dependency of the executable above -- import injection means the loader resolves it before any game code runs, so if this file is missing the client does not start at all (exit 0xC0000135, STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND). The launcher checks for it before every launch and tells the player to add an antivirus exclusion, because a real-time scanner quarantining it AFTER the sync verified it is the realistic way it goes missing. Built /MT so KERNEL32 is its only import: a 3.3.5a install has no reason to have a VC redistributable.
_note: Must stay in step with the executable above: they share the wire-magnitude codec and the native-channel frame format. Publish them together, always.
_history_0821a: 2026-08.21a: THE DIAGNOSTIC RE-AIMED, PLUS A FLOATER FLOOD VALVE. Read of 283 hours / 40 installs / 88.7M frames from #fps-telemetry established that the 08-13 cooldown-storm fix HELD (cd/sec p50=0, p90=185, against 166,000/s sustained before it) and that the instrument shipped in 14a was, as a direct consequence, measuring nothing: 956 profiler bursts fired, ALL of them on the cooldown-RATE trigger, NONE on a freeze, and 99% of them caught a client running at a median of 115 fps. The threshold comment in 14a ("below the threshold the client is comfortably past 170fps") was true when written on 08-13 and was falsified hours later by the server-side fix that followed the same measurement -- cooldown rate stopped predicting slowness and nobody re-aimed the trigger. THREE CHANGES. (1) The storm trigger now requires the client to be genuinely slow (FPS_WATCH_SLOW_FRAMES: 5 frames or fewer per 125ms poll = 40fps) as well as busy. (2) FpsProfBurst now also fires on a freeze that is still going 1.5s in (FPS_WATCH_DEEP), rate-limited to one burst a minute across both paths -- 14a declined to on the grounds that "a freeze is over long before that", which the same telemetry falsifies: 446 real in-world hangs, median 1.6s, tail to 92.3s, one every 38 minutes, and the stack shot answers "not in lua" for 426 of them, so only the instruction pointer can name them. (3) FpsProfWhere now resolves an address to module!Export+delta by walking the loaded module's own export table, because a bare ntdll RVA is unresolvable after the fact -- syscall stubs shift by 16 bytes per patch level and the uploader records the OS build with its revision zeroed. Also: a floater flood valve at 120/sec (measured free to 60/sec, 5.6x frame cost past 120, worst second on the realm 1,001), which never drops a word floater and never drops a saturated number. Attestation UNTOUCHED -- spec 0x058B902B, 300 variants, identical to 14a and 13c, so this is not a variant-set change. Collection is NARROWED, not widened: the same categories 14a disclosed, on strictly fewer occasions.
_history_0814a: 2026-08.14a: THE WIDENED FRAME DIAGNOSTIC. 13c shipped the once-a-second frame-time bucket line and it answered the first question (frames collapse with cooldown-query storms, not with pull size: 178 fps at ~5k queries/sec against 23 fps at ~150k, with FEWER units on screen). It could not answer the second -- WHOSE code -- so this build adds three things the investigation asked for: a stall watchdog that reads the Lua call stack while the client is actually frozen, a sampling profiler that takes 512 instruction-pointer samples per burst and counts where the time genuinely is, and a hooked FrameScript_SignalEvent counter. ⚠ THIS IS A WIDENING OF WHAT IS COLLECTED: the watchdog reports Lua chunk names and line numbers, so addon FILE PATHS now leave the player's machine where 13c sent only numbers. Chunks loaded from a string carry player text as their name and are reported as a bare token with the content dropped. Attestation is untouched -- spec 0x058B902B, 300 variants, identical to 13c, so this is not a variant-set change. ★ AND THE REAL LESSON OF THIS RELEASE IS NOT IN THE DLL: 13c's diagnostic was switched off less than a day later by an unrelated client bundle, because New-Manifest.ps1 defaulted fpsReportWebhook to '' and a release passes the flags it is thinking about. A null webhook does not pause collection, it deletes the logs. The generator now inherits both webhooks when the flag is absent.
_history_0809b: 2026-08.09b: CLIENT ATTESTATION. The DLL now answers a server challenge on opcode 0x513 (topic ATT) that an addon-only client cannot even receive, because 0x513 dispatches through a table only the DLL registers into. 300 generated response variants, regenerated per release. ⚠ THE INTERLOCK IS THE IMPORTANT PART: the DLL carries a plain-text marker (UNCAPPED-ATTEST-SPEC:...) and tools/attestation/check_release.py is wired into New-Manifest.ps1, which THROWS before writing the manifest if the DLL, the generated .inc, this pin and the bytes actually served do not all agree. Server and client must hold the same variant set or every player fails at once. ★ ALSO CARRIES 2026-08.09a, which was published to the host at 01:03 on 2026-08-09 and NEVER PINNED -- it sat served and unreferenced while every player kept running 08.07b. Reconstructed the pre-attestation source and diffed it against the published 09a: 6 differing bytes, both copies of the PE timestamp, so the working tree IS 09a's source and its content is carried forward here. What 09a changed versus 07b could not be determined -- ~1.4KB of .text across Hook_ItemCount/DecodeWireMagnitude/DllMain/DsRead/EnsureNetHandler, no size, string or import change, and kVaultAwareReturns byte-identical in both, so it is NOT another vault-return edit. That unpinned-DLL gap is why Launcher/tools/preflight-release.sh now exists.
_history: 2026-08.07b: hooks 0x005E2797 + 0x005E27B0, the QUEST LOG / TRACKER objective text -- "Akiris Reed: 0/10" on the mob tooltip while the Vault held 4 (quest 617, item 4029). ★ THESE ARE THE TWO ADDRESSES 07a's note calls wrong and says were removed. They are not bad addresses; they were attached to the wrong bug. 07a was chasing the greyed questgiver button, inferred these from disassembly, shipped them, saw no change, and deleted them -- correctly, since they never fire at a questgiver. But deleting them threw away the fix for a different symptom nobody had reported yet. Now observed by the diagnostic with the symptom on screen: 'UNHOOKED site ret=005E2797 item=4029 bags=0 vault=4' and the same for 005E27B0, two adjacent sites in one tick as the objective text builds have-vs-need. The rule stands (observe, do not infer) with an addition: an address that fails to fix the symptom you are holding is not thereby a bad address -- check what it DOES fire on before deleting it. 2026-08.07a: hooks 0x0058CBFB, the QUESTGIVER DIALOG's required-item check -- report #239, the greyed Continue/Complete button when the quest's items were in the Vault. The client runs that check itself before any packet is sent, so no server change could reach it; auto-accept/auto-complete completing the same turn-in while the button stayed dead is what proved it was client-side. Verified in-game before publishing: 'HOOKED site ret=0058CBFB item=11316 bags=0 vault=1 -> 1', Continue enabled, quest handed in. ⚠ The executable is NOT republished alongside this one despite the note above: that rule guards the shared wire codec and frame format, and this change touches neither -- it only adds an entry to kVaultAwareReturns. Two earlier guesses (0x005E2797 / 0x005E27B0), inferred from disassembly rather than observed, never fire at a questgiver and were removed.
_cleared_20260809: Repinned to 09b after the lockout was traced to its ACTUAL cause: a startup query in item_treasure_sacks.cpp (the quest-gear sack pool) used WHERE entry IN (<10-way UNION>), which MySQL re-evaluated per row of item_template and never finished, starving the world-DB connection pool.
